review.summary: The supplied change meets the stated scope. Named statuses (400/403/429/404/503) keep their messages, any other defined status gets neutral retry guidance without network advice, and a no-status rejection keeps the network advice. I found no BLOCKER or MAJOR defects. Two low-severity observations remain. The `status !== undefined` guard also treats 0 and NaN as HTTP responses, and the tests cover only the helper, not the call sites that must pass `response.status`. No tests were run; this review is based only on the supplied text.

findings.issue: The guard treats any defined value, including 0 or NaN, as a received HTTP response. A caller that passes a sentinel such as 0 for a failed/opaque fetch would show "server rejected" neutral text instead of network guidance.
findings.evidence: `if (status !== undefined) return "資料暫時無法送出；內容仍保留，請稍後再試。";` The tests exercise only 409/422/500/502/504 and `undefined`; no 0/NaN case.
findings.impact: Low. Real fetch rejections throw rather than yield status 0, so this only matters if a call site normalizes a missing status to 0 or NaN. The result would be network advice mistakenly suppressed.
findings.recommended_fix: Treat only valid HTTP statuses as present, e.g. `if (Number.isInteger(status) && status >= 100) ...`. Otherwise fall through to the network message. Alternatively, document that callers must pass `undefined` for transport failures.
findings.required_test: Assert that `formSubmissionErrorMessage(0)` and `formSubmissionErrorMessage(NaN)` return the network-check message, if the stricter guard is adopted.

findings.file: Call sites of postRegistrationSubmission / formSubmissionErrorMessage (not supplied)
findings.area: Integration of status propagation (outside supplied scope)
findings.issue: The new neutral message only takes effect if call sites pass `response.status` on non-OK responses. The supplied tests cover the helper in isolation, so they cannot show that a caller does not call `formSubmissionErrorMessage()` without a status after an HTTP failure, for example in a catch block after a JSON parse error.
findings.evidence: Only the helper and its unit tests were supplied. The original MINOR concerned HTTP failures being given network advice, which depends on caller behavior.
findings.impact: If any caller omits the status on an HTTP error, users would still see the misleading network advice. This cannot be confirmed or ruled out from the supplied text.
findings.recommended_fix: Have the callers read `response.status` before any body parsing. Pass it to `formSubmissionErrorMessage` for every `!response.ok` result, and pass `undefined` only when `fetch` rejects.
findings.required_test: Add a component or integration test with a mocked `fetch` resolving to `{ ok: false, status: 500, json: () => Promise.reject(...) }`, asserting the rendered message lacks "網路". Add one with `fetch` rejecting, asserting it contains "檢查網路".
